sections.h2: Selling in Brownsville at a glance
sections.html:
Brownsville sits on the Rio Grande, facing Matamoros, and serves as the seat of Cameron County. Most sales involve three local offices: the appraisal district, the clerk and the tax office. Population was estimated at 192,957 in mid-2025, 3.6% above the 2020 base. Owner-occupants hold 61.7% of the homes, which carry a median value of $139,900. Median rent runs $923.

Because 83.6% of residents over age five speak another language at home, contracts here are often read in two languages. Everyone on the deed should understand the paper before signing it.

sections.h2: How Cameron CAD sets your value
sections.html:
The Cameron Appraisal District puts a number on your house, and every taxing unit then picks its own rate. Expect a fresh appraisal at least once in any three-year span, sooner where prices are jumping.

Raise a value by $1,000 or less and the district owes no notice, so some owners never see a mailing. Section 23.23 of the Tax Code has limited a homestead's assessed value to 10% yearly growth since January 1, 2008. New rooms, pools and similar improvements fall outside the limit.

You prove Texas residency with something like a driver's license. Married owners each apply and show ID. A residence can carry the homestead, over-65, disabled person or 100% disabled veteran exemption. The disabled veteran exemption alternatively attaches to any one property that veteran owns.

  • You can claim over-65 or disabled in a given year, not both.
  • If some owners live elsewhere, the account splits, and the exemption shrinks to the qualifying owner's share.
  • Adding a pool, garage or room raises the school tax ceiling. A Tax Ceiling Transfer form carries it to a new Texas homestead.

A few exemption types need a new application by April 30 each year. Ask the district which ones apply to you.

Protests must be written. They are due on whichever date is later, May 15 or the thirtieth day after your notice arrived. You may mail, hand-deliver or email, though mail must be postmarked in time.

After the deadline, the district and the review board lose the power to change the value. Hospitalization can excuse a late filing. Forgetting cannot. File on time and you receive at least 15 days' notice of a hearing that tends to last about 15 minutes. If the ruling still seems wrong, you can sue in district court, request binding arbitration, or, in Cameron County, appeal to the State Office of Administrative Hearings.

  • Give your name and the address or account number of the property.
  • State the issue, such as market value.
  • Attach comparable sales, photos or repair estimates as support.

January 1 fixes both value and the tax lien. The county tax office shares an East Levee Street address with the clerk. Call to find out which taxing units bill your house and what you owe.

Key dates for a Brownsville property tax bill
WhenEvent for the owner
January 1The year's value is fixed and the lien attaches
April 30Some exemption types need a new application
May 15, or day 30 after the noticeLast day to protest, whichever falls later
Around October 1Bills arrive
February 1Balances still owed become delinquent: six percent penalty, one percent interest
After July 1Twelve percent penalty; the taxing unit's lawyer may tack on up to 20 percent

Clear title is impossible with delinquent tax on the books, so pay any balance by closing.

sections.h2: What if the property is headed for a tax sale?
sections.html:
Tax sales are auctions conducted by a constable or a hired agent. No statewide list exists. Look for notices on county websites.

What an owner can recover depends on the property type. For homestead, farm or mineral land, the owner may redeem for two years after the buyer's deed is filed, paying 25% over in year one or 50% over in year two, plus costs. All other property gets 180 days and up to 25% over. Any surplus from the sale is yours to claim for two years after the sale.

Valley family land often remains titled to a relative who died decades ago. The quick fix is an affidavit of heirship, sworn and filed with the county clerk. Nobody in court reviews it, though, and a title insurer can turn it down.

Sturdier options: open probate within four years; use a muniment of title when the estate owes only liens on the real estate; or rely on a transfer on death deed recorded while the owner lived. An heir who is not on the recorded deed can still seek an exemption. The appraisal district wants an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate and a recent utility bill.

sections.h2: Where a Brownsville deed is recorded
sections.html:
Visit the Cameron County Clerk at 835 E. Levee Street for deeds, liens, plats and maps. After a deed is recorded, bring Cameron CAD the instrument, or its volume and page numbers, so the owner of record gets updated.

The state clerk manual lists $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each additional page, plus other fees. Call the clerk for what your deed will cost.

Pick the route by looking at the house itself, not by what a neighbor did. A tidy home can draw several buyers who need mortgages, but you wait on appraisals and lender calendars. A home with an aging roof, a stubborn tenant or years of unpaid tax suits a buyer who pays cash, accepts the problems and closes once title work clears.

Compare offers on price, closing costs and closing date, side by side, and have the title company check that no tax or lien item changes the numbers. If two offers land close together, the faster and cleaner closing is usually worth more than a small difference in price, since each extra week means another month of taxes, insurance and upkeep on a house you are trying to leave.

Open a folder before you call anyone. Inside, keep the latest county tax bill, the appraisal notice if one came, and the Cameron CAD account number with its exemption list. Loan payoff letter, lease, probate papers or recorded affidavit go in too, whichever apply. Ask the clerk whether liens or old instruments are filed against the property, because a lien found late stalls a closing.

Before any money moves, the title company gets the tax balance, runs a lien search and works out which signatures are needed. It settles any mortgage with the payoff figure. For an inherited house, the probate or affidavit route has to be sorted out first. The deed is then signed, acknowledged and recorded by the county clerk.

Your homestead exemption stays with you, so a buyer who intends to live there applies for a new one. Ask the clerk's office for copies of the recorded deed once it is filed, and keep them with your sale papers. If someone is still in the house, settle a move-out date with the buyer before you sign the contract.

faqs.q: What does a typical Brownsville home cost?
faqs.a: Median value for an owner-occupied home is $139,900, but condition, lot and street move any single sale up or down.

faqs.q: Will Cameron CAD always mail a value notice?
faqs.a: No. A notice goes out only when the law calls for one, and an increase of $1,000 or less needs none.

faqs.q: When is a Brownsville appraisal protest due?
faqs.a: By the later of May 15 and 30 days after delivery of the notice. It must be written, and you may mail it, bring it in or email it.

faqs.q: Where can I get a copy of my Brownsville deed?
faqs.a: Go to the county clerk on East Levee Street. The appraisal district does not hand out deeds, surveys or plats.

faqs.q: Does a Brownsville homeowner over 65 get a tax ceiling?
faqs.a: Yes. School taxes on the home usually stay flat for as long as you own and live in it, and the ceiling can follow you to a new Texas homestead.
